title: Text back every missed call within a minute
one_liner: When a call goes unanswered, the caller gets a friendly text right away asking what they need, and you get the reply with a suggested next step.
steps: Your phone system flags a missed call and sends the caller's number to the workflow.
The AI writes a short, human-sounding text that names your business and asks what they need and when.
The reply lands in your CRM or inbox with a summary and a suggested booking time.
You or your front desk take it from there; the AI never quotes prices or promises availability.
guardrail: A person reviews every reply and makes all pricing and scheduling commitments; the AI only opens the conversation and stops after one message unless the customer replies.
tools: Twilio or your existing business phone (OpenPhone, RingCentral), n8n or Make, an LLM (Claude or OpenAI), your CRM (HubSpot, GoHighLevel, Jobber)
prompt: You write text messages for [business name], a [type of business] in [city]. A caller just missed us at [time]. Write one friendly SMS under 300 characters that: says sorry we missed the call, asks what they need help with, and offers to find a time that works. Do not quote prices, promise availability, or mention AI. Sound like a real person at the front desk. Return only the message text.
source_name: vantaige.io n8n blueprints / Contra portfolio (missed-call SMS pattern)
verify_note: Expected: a single warm SMS under 300 chars, asking what they need, no prices or promises.

title: Remind customers before the job, rebook them after
one_liner: Each scheduled job triggers a reminder with prep details the day before, then a thank-you and a rebooking nudge a few days after.
steps: A job is scheduled in your field-service or booking tool.
The AI drafts a reminder using the job type, date, and prep instructions you provide.
After the job is marked complete, a thank-you goes out with a simple way to book the next visit.
Customers who reply with a question or complaint are routed to a person, not answered by the AI.
guardrail: Templates are approved by you once up front, and any reply that isn't a simple confirmation goes to a human.
tools: Jobber, Housecall Pro or Calendly, Zapier or Make, an LLM (Claude or OpenAI), SMS or email
prompt: You write customer messages for [business name], a [type of service] company. Write two short messages for a [job type] scheduled on [date] at [time]. Message 1 is a reminder for the day before: confirm the time, list this prep: [prep steps], and say how to reschedule: [reschedule method]. Message 2 is sent [number] days after the job: thank them, ask if everything went well, and offer to book their next [recommended repeat service]. Tone: friendly and plain. No discounts, prices, or guarantees. Return both messages labeled.
source_name: Housecall Pro help center (automated job reminders and follow-ups)
verify_note: Expected: two labeled, short messages with the placeholders filled in, no invented offers.

title: Win back customers who haven't booked in a while
one_liner: AI finds customers whose last service was long enough ago to be due again and drafts a personal check-in for each segment.
steps: Export customers with their last service type and date from your CRM or scheduling tool.
Group them by service type and how long it has been since the last visit.
The AI drafts one short message per group that references the service they had and when it is typically due.
You approve the drafts, then they send by email or text to people who opted in.
guardrail: You approve every draft and the list before anything sends, and only customers who agreed to hear from you are included.
tools: Jobber, Housecall Pro or your CRM, Google Sheets, Make or Zapier, an LLM (Claude or OpenAI), Mailchimp or Klaviyo or SMS
prompt: You write marketing messages for [business name], a [type of business] in [city]. Write a short email (under 90 words) for customers whose last [service type] was about [time since last service] ago. Mention that [service type] is usually due every [interval], invite them to book at [booking link], and sound like a neighbor, not an ad. Do not invent discounts, deadlines, or claims. Use [first name] as a placeholder. Return a subject line and the body.
verify_note: Expected: subject plus an under-90-word email with the placeholders intact and no invented offers.

title: Turn finished-job photos into ready-to-review posts
one_liner: Drop in photos and a two-line job note, and AI drafts a local-flavored post for your Google profile and social pages for you to approve.
steps: After a job, the crew uploads photos and a short note to a shared form or Drive folder.
The AI drafts a caption that names the service and neighborhood from the note.
The draft is sent to you for approval.
Approved posts are published, or posted by hand if your tool can't post directly.
guardrail: Nothing posts without approval, and customers' names, addresses, and faces are never included unless they've given permission.
tools: Google Forms or Drive, n8n or Make, an LLM (Claude or OpenAI), Google Business Profile, Facebook/Instagram via Zernio or Buffer
prompt: You write social posts for [business name], a [type of business] in [city]. Using this job note: [job note, no customer names or addresses], write (1) a Google Business Profile post under 120 words and (2) an Instagram caption under 60 words. Mention the service and the general area [neighborhood or town] only. Include a plain call to action: [call to action]. Do not invent results, numbers, or reviews. Return both, labeled.
source_name: n8n social automation templates and freelancer briefs (photo + caption + approval pattern)
verify_note: Expected: two labeled posts with the service and town mentioned, a CTA, and no fabricated results.
